purpose: Bisoprolol is mainly used to treat high blood pressure and heart failure. Keeping blood pressure under control helps lower your risk of heart attacks, strokes, and kidney problems. Your doctor may also prescribe it to help your heart beat more steadily and efficiently.
how_it_works: Your heart has special receptors that respond to stress hormones like adrenaline, which can make your heart beat faster and harder. Bisoprolol blocks those receptors, so your heart slows down a little and does not have to work as hard. Think of it like taking your heart from a high speed down to a comfortable, steady pace.
common_side_effects: You might feel tired or a little dizzy, especially when you first start taking it. Some people notice cold hands or feet, or feel slightly short of breath. Occasionally it can cause headaches, nausea, or slow heartbeat. Most of these tend to improve as your body adjusts.
warnings: Never stop taking bisoprolol suddenly without talking to your doctor first — stopping abruptly can cause your heart rate and blood pressure to spike dangerously. Tell your doctor if you have asthma, diabetes, or slow heart rate, as bisoprolol may not be the best choice or may need close monitoring. It can also hide some signs of low blood sugar if you are a diabetic on insulin.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 2.5 to 5 mg taken once daily by mouth, in the morning. Your doctor may gradually increase it up to 10 mg or sometimes 20 mg per day depending on your condition and how well you respond. Always take it at the same time each day, with or without food.
